generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, this means running the same process on every assignment, whether it is a coaching plan, a lab report or a management essay. You read the brief for its steer and keywords and plan, you get a rough draft down, and then you edit it for structure and clarity. A coach and a physiologist write about different things, but they work through the same stages. Making this your normal way of working is what steadily improves your sport writing.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students each have a report on a training programme to write. Tom writes it in one sitting, straight to the finished version, with no plan and no time to revise, so his points end up in a confusing order. Amara works through the whole process: she reads the brief and plans, drafts quickly, then edits her structure and sentences before proofreading. Both knew the programme, but Amara's report is clearer and better organised, because it went through every stage.
generatedProse.summary: Academic writing in the School of Sport is most useful when you treat it as one process, not three separate skills. You run the same stages in order on every assignment: understand the brief, plan, draft, then revise for the basics. Making this your normal way of working is what steadily improves your sport writing.

check.body: A student reads a task closely and plans, writes a rough first draft, then edits it for structure and clarity before proofreading. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the student is using the whole writing process: each stage leads into the next, from task to finished piece.
_items.feedback: Yes. Every stage is there, in order, working as one process.

_items.text: That the student is wasting time by doing more than one piece of writing needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each stage does a different job, and together they make the piece stronger.

_items.text: That only the proofreading at the end really matters.
_items.feedback: Not so. The earlier stages did the real work, and proofreading only polishes the surface.

_items.text: That planning and editing are the same stage.
_items.feedback: They are different stages: planning comes before the draft, and editing improves it afterwards.
